info.summary: Bulk volunteer shift operations for the Rose City Rollers.
info.title: star-pass

get.description:
The settings collections use, as the service read them at startup. To change a setting or a credential, edit its value in your `.env` file and restart `star-pass`.

Lists the calendars a collection request may name.
get.summary: Report what the service was configured with

post.description:
Reads one event from each configured calendar, and indicates whether or not each read was successful. The key's last four characters are visible in the response. To change the key, edit its value in your `.env` file and restart `star-pass`.

Each calendar produces its own result because Google's API may successfully authenticate a key and determine the key is not authorized for a calendar. A refused key is a result, not an error.

The API rate limits this test per caller, separately from the Amplify test. A request over the limit receives a `429` with a `Retry-After` header, and does not reach Google.

Stores no data and takes no idempotency key.
post.summary: Test the League Calendar key this service is running on

post.description:
Sends one read request to Amplify, and indicates whether or not Amplify accepted the token. The token's last four characters are visible in the response. To change the token, edit its value in your `.env` file and restart `star-pass`.

A refused token is a result, not an application error.

The API rate limits this test per caller. A request over the limit receives a `429` with a `Retry-After` header, and does not reach Amplify.

Stores no data and takes no idempotency key.
post.summary: Test the Amplify credential this service is running on

A server-sent event stream. Each frame is named for what the job reported, and contains that report. The stream ends with a `job_finished` frame.

To reconnect, send the identifier of the last frame received in `Last-Event-ID`. The stream continues after that frame. A browser sends this header automatically.

post.description:
Runs an interrupted job again. A job is interrupted when the process running it stops before the job ends. When the service starts, it marks any queued or running job as interrupted.

You may only resume an interrupted job, and only while no other job is working on the same run.

A resumed send creates only the shifts Amplify does not have. The job keeps its identifier. Its start time, end time, and failure reason are cleared.

post.description:
Collects a calendar's events in a date range into a new run, ready to review.

Answers when the run is created, with the job that collects the events. To follow its progress, read the job or its event stream. The run appears in the run list immediately.

The date range is a first day and the day after the last day, in the service's time zone, with no length limit. An event with no opportunity is collected, and blocks the send.

You may not delete a run that is collecting events, is sending shifts to Amplify, or already sent shifts to Amplify.

patch.description:
One user action, as a list of operations: set the category, set a shift start or end, set a role's volunteer count, nudge, reset volunteer counts, remove events, or undo an event's changes.

An action over several rows is one request, one change log entry, and one revision change. The operations apply in order, and each sees the result of the previous operation.

**The service applies the entire request or none of it.** If an operation would leave an event unable to become a correct shift, the service refuses the request and writes no changes.

`set_start` and `set_end` set the **shift** times sent to Amplify. `undo` restores an event's collected opportunity, shift times, and volunteer count.

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry with the same key receives the first answer. A key sent with different operations is refused.

post.description:
Adds an uncollected event to the run's current revision, by its identifier in the run's uncollected list.

**Only an event with the `search` reason may be added**: an event no search term returned. Events excluded by title, all-day events, and untitled events are refused. An event already in the revision is also refused, so a repeated request does not add a duplicate row.

The added event is matched and timed the same way a collected event is, and is marked as manually added. Reverting to revision 1 removes the event and returns it to the uncollected list.

If the event has an Amplify opportunity the run has not read, the service reads its title from Amplify.

Answers with the current revision.

get.description:
Shifts a send would create in Amplify for each opportunity, the shifts already in Amplify, and the reasons any events may not be sent to Amplify. Several categories may share one opportunity.

Shifts are counted by need ID, date, start, and end. Two events that would create the same shift count once.

An event that cannot become a shift blocks the entire send. A blocking event is listed once for each reason.

The service reads every opportunity from Amplify to answer. A send checks Amplify again before it writes.

post.description:
Replaces the run's events with the current League Calendar events, from the same calendar and date range. The run keeps its identifier and date range. A new revision contains the new events, and earlier revisions remain readable.

**Collecting a run again discards any changes made to it since it was collected.** Set `expectedChangeCount` to the number of changes `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/revisions` reports for the current revision. If the number does not match, the run is not collected again.

You may not collect a run again while another job is working on it, or after it sent shifts to Amplify.

post.description:
Restores the events of an earlier revision by adding a new revision that copies it. Editing continues in the new revision.

Reverting does not change any other revision. To undo a revert, revert to the revision that was current before it.

Reverting to revision 1 removes manually added events and returns them to the run's uncollected list.

Answers with the full run.

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry with the same key receives the first answer. A key sent with a different revision number is refused.

post.description:
Creates every shift in the run's current revision that Amplify does not have. **Sending creates shifts in Amplify, and it may not be undone.**

Set `expectedShiftCount` to the preview's `totals.willCreate`. If there are changes to the run or Amplify shifts after the preview, the send is refused. Read the preview again to see the current number of shifts.

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry with the same key receives the first answer. A key sent with a different `expectedShiftCount` is refused.

Before writing to each opportunity, the service reads the opportunity from Amplify and skips the shifts it already has. The service sends one request per opportunity. If a request's answer does not arrive, the run is `partly_sent`, and sending again creates only the missing shifts.

Answers when the job is created.

You may not send a run while another job is working on it, while it is being collected, or while any event in it is blocking.

get.description:
One entry per title and calendar, newest to oldest, with the number of sightings and when the title was first and last seen. Each run the title appears in adds one sighting, and so does each manually recorded sighting.

A title that appears routinely is likely a category missing from the data model. A title seen once may be a one-time event.

Any unmatched titles from a run remain in the log after the run is deleted.
get.summary: List titles the data model has not matched

post.description:
Records one sighting of a title found outside a collection. Collections record their own sightings.

A title recorded twice with no run is two sightings in one entry. A run counts each title once, so a retry that names the same run adds no sighting.

Answers with the updated entry.

The calendar must be one the deployment configured. The run is optional. Any unmatched titles from a run remain in the log after the run is deleted.

Takes no `Idempotency-Key`.
post.summary: Record a title the data model did not match
